conflicts.description: V288 and V159 require the ESC pack switch to open within the 500 ms stop deadline after a motor overcurrent or over-temperature detection. The detection chain reaches the main coprocessor in about 18 ms (INA228 ALERT within 17.0 ms, 74VHC21FT 8.5 ns, 1 ms pass; the MCP9808 at the onboard shunt 60 to 500 ms by resolution) and the coprocessor disarms its outputs. The pack switch drivers (TPSI3052DWZR) take the latch output alone: no coprocessor input exists (V53, V160), the Not defeatable rule allows none, and docs/Safety.md states that no hardware covers a healthy panel with a misbehaving coprocessor. The switch opens only when the panel's heartbeat stops (enable falls 155 to 185 ms later, switch open within 5 ms), and no coprocessor action stops it. A path through the panel (fault bit read at a 50 ms poll, STOP, heartbeat) adds up to 17 + 20 + 50 + 185 + 5 = 277 ms plus a panel reaction time that no page defines.

assumptions.value: 2 PIO state machines on the measurement coprocessor, both in PIO1: 1 receive and 1 transmit, 13 instruction words (UART receive 9 + transmit 4, sized from the pico-examples UART programs, which are not in the tree); one receiver input on GPIO 23 (V68); the receive program takes the S.BUS 8E2 100 kbaud frame with the pad's input inversion and the other buses (iBUS, SUMD, CRSF, SRXL2, JETI EX Bus) as UART; the transmit state machine drives GPIO 23 through SN74LVC1T45DBVR, whose direction pin takes 1 more GPIO (counted in GPIO: measurement). A hardware UART is available for the receive-only buses: UART1 is free on this chip and GPIO 23 has UART1_RX (funcsel 0x0b), but UART1_TX would need GPIO 20, 22, 24 or 26, which the encoder, the chip select and the TCA9548A reset hold, so the transmit direction needs PIO.
assumptions.why: No receiver PIO program is written (docs/Receivers.md); V71 (owner, 2026-09-28) says the bench transmits on a receiver input for JETI EX Bus and SRXL2; the map puts the receiver on PIO1; the count must be stated and the count for transmit is the smallest that meets V71.
